domains.label: principles
domains.title: Guiding principles & source-of-truth discipline
domains.verdict: Mostly disciplined and self-aware — the architecture's core promises (vault-as-truth, Copilot-only egress, thin renderer, rebuildable/labeled caches) are genuinely honored in code — but discipline erodes at the seams where two features solve the same read-caching problem independently, where a spec's own requirement IDs collide, and where a "must" product principle (headless background operation) silently applies to only one OS.
domains.summary:
This domain asked whether KB-App's code honors its own stated values and whether there are duplicate or conflicting sources of truth. The headline finding is genuinely positive: the renderer boundary is clean — zero electron/require/raw-fetch calls found anywhere in shell/ or qcap/, and preload.ts is a thin 102-line passthrough exposing exactly the typed KbApi surface. Egress is tightly gated: the only raw node http/https usage in the entire 165-file engine is researchFetch.ts's SSRF-gated fetch (DNS-lookup guarded), used exclusively by the explicitly-approved public-web Researcher; M365/WorkIQ route through a read-only stdio MCP server (workiqMcp.ts) with an explicit no-send/no-write tool allowlist. The newest cache layer — the SQLite/FTS5 library index (kb/libraryIndex.ts) — has a genuinely well-reasoned freshness model (HEAD-diff incremental refresh, schema-versioned, full-rebuild fallback on any diff failure) and is correctly gitignored under .kb/cache/ with an explicit "not ground truth" comment, verified never committed in the observed vault. The prior deep review's 12-ad-hoc-walker sprawl was real, completed work: walkVaultFiles now serves 9 call sites from one implementation.

Where discipline breaks down is at points of unreconciled overlap between features that solved the same problem twice, independently. Explore reads a 5-second-cadence, full-vault-walk, in-memory GraphProjection; Health and Ask instead read the SQLite index. SPEC-0058's STATE-3 requirement explicitly says Health "reads the same graph projection" as Explore — that is not what shipped, and neither spec was updated to reconcile: SPEC-0058 remains unedited on this point, and healthView.ts's own comment admits "kb:healthReport is still a per-read scan, not projection-backed." A byte-identical extractWikilinks() parser is deliberately triplicated across recallTools.ts, graphProjection.ts, and libraryIndexBuild.ts — each comment explains this was a wave-1 concurrency-avoidance tradeoff (avoid editing a parallel-owned file) that, unlike the analogous walker sprawl, never got its own cleanup epic. Most concretely, SPEC-0058's own problem statement named "registry list views (jobs/researchers/sources/settings) read off staging with no coordination → torn-read/race hazard" as a confirmed offender; three of its four fellow offenders (Explore, Health/Ask, Activity) were fixed via projections/caches, but the registries were not — listJobsForActive, listResearchersForActive, and listWatchFoldersForActive all still call straight into unlocked, uncached reads (readJobRegistry, readInstanceConfig, N per-job readJournal calls) off active.stagingWt, the exact tree the canonical-writer lock concurrently mutates. This is the one originally-diagnosed defect from SPEC-0058 that was never actually slotted (Slice 4 was never built), left exactly where the 07-12 review found it, seven weeks into a frozen main.

The most consequential finding is platform-scoped: VISION-10 ("must: the app runs headless — orchestration, recurring jobs, polling, agents — with no window open") and SPEC-0003's own experience-surface table ("Headless daemon... background, always-on") are honored only on macOS. lifecycle.ts's shouldQuitOnWindowAllClosed() returns true for every platform except darwin, and main.ts's own comment states plainly that "on macOS the app stays alive with no window open... other platforms quit as usual." On Windows — a platform nightly CI explicitly tests as a shipped e2e/package target — closing the last window fully terminates the process: no background pipeline, no scheduled Librarian/researcher work, no watched-folder ingestion, no proactive intake, and the renderer surfaces zero messaging telling a Windows user this is happening. This is corroborated by the still-open daemon RFC (#531, filed 07-12, unresolved) which itself names "headless-run is a ratified product requirement" as unaddressed architecture debt.

A smaller but revealing self-consistency bug: SPEC-0011 (the canonical, "active"-status engineering-rules doc, whose own SPECSYS-1 in SPEC-0000 mandates stable, unique requirement IDs) defines ENG-7 twice, as two unrelated rules (a dependency-adoption rule under E1, and a "stories need addressable requirements" rule under E2). This is not merely cosmetic: nine shipped files (main/pipeline.ts plus eight main/registries/*.ts files) cite "#528 ENG-7" as the rationale for a god-file decomposition refactor that matches neither definition verbatim — live evidence the collision already produced unverifiable traceability, the exact failure mode SPEC-0000 says the ID system exists to prevent. Relatedly, 69 of 87 spec files (79%) remain status: draft — including the two most foundational and most-implemented product specs, SPEC-0001 (ubiquitous language) and SPEC-0007 (core data model) — and SPEC-0000, the meta-spec governing the lifecycle, never defines graduation criteria for status beyond a bare inline comment in TEMPLATE.md ("draft | active | deprecated | superseded"), so status is not functioning as an enforced gate. In the other direction, SPEC-0061's REFIT-1/REFIT-2 (Health-and-Ask-read-an-index) are marked Verify: none-yet in a draft spec whose own preface calls its IDs "not yet committed," yet both are fully shipped in ipc.ts — architecture is outrunning its own spec's paper trail in both directions at once. Finally, the observed instance shows real symptom of a config-surface gap noted only in passing: package.json's internal name ("kb-app") diverged from productName ("Vellum") across the product's renames, appConfig.ts has no migration logic for prior userData directories, and the live instance carries three orphaned userData trees (kb-app/KB-App/vellum) — a concrete, low-effort gap in an otherwise well-organized set of ~8 distinct, clearly-commented config surfaces (app-global activeVaultPath, per-vault instance.json, four registries, directives, shipped Obsidian config).

strengths: Renderer/main boundary is clean and enforced in practice, not just by convention: zero electron/require/fetch/WebSocket references anywhere in shell/ or qcap/; preload.ts is a thin 102-line passthrough to the typed KbApi (kb/types.ts), matching the 'same surface a daemon would expose' goal named in the review brief.

Copilot-only egress principle is genuinely narrow and well-gated: the entire engine's only raw network code is researchFetch.ts's single SSRF-gated fetch (DNS-lookup guarded via a custom http/https Agent), used exclusively by the explicitly-approved public-web Researcher; M365/WorkIQ integrations route through a read-only stdio MCP server (workiqMcp.ts) with an explicit no-send/no-write tool allowlist and a documented outbound-query-only egress model (buildOutboundQuery — never raw KB content).

The SQLite/FTS5 library index (kb/libraryIndex.ts, libraryIndexSqlite.ts) is a well-designed rebuildable cache: HEAD-gated freshness check (cheap no-op on the common case), incremental git-diff apply with automatic full-rebuild fallback on any diff failure, schema-versioned, and correctly excluded from the vault's git history via a labeled '.kb/cache/ ... not ground truth' .gitignore entry (confirmed never committed in the observed vault's history).

Real, verifiable progress on a named prior debt item: the 12 ad-hoc recursive vault walkers flagged by the 07-12 deep review were consolidated into one shared walkVaultFiles() helper, now used by 9 call sites across claimsStage/graphProjection/libraryIndexBuild/connectStage/reviewStore/mergeNodes/recallTools/recall/enrichTrigger.

Config surfaces that do exist are individually well-organized: each config-owning file (instanceConfig.ts, watchRegistry.ts, obsidianConfig.ts) carries an explicit, specific comment explaining why that setting lives where it does and why it is deliberately kept separate from neighboring surfaces (e.g., instanceConfig.ts: 'Deliberately kept OUT of the core VaultConfig / SPEC-0007 data model').

Where a knob genuinely has multiple sources (the Copilot concurrency ceiling: env var, manual Settings, cores-derived Auto), the precedence is explicit, documented, and deliberately layered (env > Settings > Auto) rather than silently conflicting — a positive counter-example to the unreconciled-cache findings elsewhere in this report.

Activity (SPEC-0058 STATE-4) is genuinely shipped as specified: kb:activityFeed calls loadActivityIndex (the HEAD-keyed cache), not buildActivityIndex (the full rebuild) — the one 'confirmed offender' from SPEC-0058's original problem list that was fixed exactly as the spec prescribed.

macOS-only OS integrations (Accessibility-gated capture context, Screen-Recording TCC status) degrade gracefully and explicitly to 'unsupported'/'denied' off-darwin rather than crashing or silently misbehaving — the right pattern for principle (f), in contrast to the headless-quitting gap which degrades silently with no such signal.
open_questions: Was the Explore-vs-Health/Ask dual-graph-cache split (finding PRIN-3) a deliberate architectural decision ratified by KB-Lead/Principal when #530 shipped, or an unreviewed side-effect of parallel wave-1 lanes? If deliberate, SPEC-0058 STATE-3 should be formally superseded rather than left silently unmet.

Is Windows actually intended as a v1-shipped platform, or is nightly.yml's 'macOS + Windows' e2e/package matrix aspirational/leftover scaffolding? This materially changes whether PRIN-1 (headless is macOS-only) is release-blocking.

Does the Principal (the sole user/tester so far, per the observed single instance) actually run this on Windows/Linux at all today, or has the headless-only-on-macOS gap simply never been exercised in practice?
What is the actual next free requirement-ID slot in SPEC-0011 for the ENG-7 renumbering (PRIN-5) — the spec excerpt read this session didn't show IDs above ENG-16.

domains.label: tests
domains.title: Test coverage (semantic, requirement-traced)
domains.verdict: A genuinely strong mechanism-level suite (3097 unit tests, real injectable-runner decider tests, no assertion-free/snapshot/locale-fragile smells) sits on top of a traceability layer and a nightly signal path that have both quietly rotted — roughly half of all MUST requirements still read "Verify: none-yet" (some falsely stale, some honestly unbuilt, indistinguishably), 3 of 12 e2e specs have been broken since their view's v3 rebuild landed, and the automation meant to surface exactly that kind of drift (nightly + report-red) has been silently broken for its entire 7-week life.
domains.summary:
The unit/component tier (Vitest, 253 files / 3097 tests, green in 98s) is the healthiest part of this domain. The injectable-runner pattern for the six Copilot deciders (`deciderScaffold.ts`'s `CopilotRunner` seam, consumed by `makeDecomposeDecider` et al.) genuinely exercises real prompt-building/JSON-parsing/validation logic and only swaps the process-spawn boundary — `vi.mock` is used sparingly (24 files) and mostly to assert a real regression guard (subprocess `cwd` scoping, the COPILOT-CONTEXT-SCOPE-BUG). A repo-wide sweep found zero assertion-free test files, zero unit-tier snapshot tests, and zero remaining `toLocaleString()`-based date assertions — the prior review's locale-fragility class appears fully remediated. The component tier, formally "reserved" by SPEC-0012 TEST-5, is in practice active in 27 files via a per-file `@vitest-environment happy-dom` pragma — the team simply never went back to graduate TEST-5's own status.

Where it breaks down is traceability and the nightly signal path, and the two compound each other. Parsing every requirements table in specs/ (687 rows with a Priority + Verify column) shows 360 rows (52%) still say `Verify: none-yet`, including 250 of 506 MUST rows (49%). Separately, of 755 unique requirement IDs defined anywhere in specs/, 334 (44%) are never referenced by ID in any `*.test.ts`/`*.e2e.ts`/`*.eval.ts` file — TEST-14's "SHOULD name the requirement ID" convention is followed inconsistently. Critically, these two numbers conflate two very different situations that a reader currently cannot tell apart: SPEC-0060 (the fully-shipped v3 UI overhaul across all 10 views) carries 16/16 MUST requirements at `none-yet`, yet 11 of those exact IDs (VUX-1,3,4,6,10,11,13,14,16,17,19) are explicitly named in `describe()` titles in `exploreView.test.ts`, `askView.test.ts`, `healthView.test.ts` and others — the spec's bookkeeping was simply never graduated (a TEST-15 violation at scale), not a coverage gap. By contrast, SPEC-0035 Health's HEALTH-2 through HEALTH-9 (causality-ordered auto-fix, REFLECT-routed judgment queue, fix audit, protected-node guard) are genuinely `none-yet` — the only remediation that shipped (`healthRemediation.ts`, relink + find-homes) is a narrower slice filed under a different spec (SPEC-0060 VUX-16) that never cross-referenced or partially-graduated SPEC-0035.

The three e2e specs the nightly matrix has failed on since 07-13 (`activity.e2e.ts`, `ask.e2e.ts`, `jobs.e2e.ts`) are all confirmed test-drift, not product regressions, and a live nightly run pulled this session (2026-09-04, run 33845332067) reproduces exactly this: 9 passed / 3 failed on both macOS and Windows, same 3 specs both times. Each one stopped being touched the moment its view got a v3 rebuild: `activity.e2e.ts` (last touched 06-02) asserts `.activity-empty`, replaced 07-12 by the shared `emptyState()` primitive (`.viz-empty`, #575); `ask.e2e.ts` (last touched 06-02) asserts `.ask-citations .cite-ref` and a raw vault-path tooltip, both replaced by the v3 Ask rebuild (#484, mid-June) — the tooltip assertion in particular now contradicts a *deliberate* later fix (#522 VUX-CLIP C6, which intentionally stopped showing the raw ref as a terminology-leak fix); `jobs.e2e.ts` asserts `.agents-hub-title`, which the v3 Agents-hub rebuild (#486) replaced with a plain `<h1>`. Tellingly, the fix for exactly this class of brittleness was already invented and applied once — `smoke.e2e.ts` deliberately moved off an exact-copy-string assertion (#527 ENG-15) onto `data-testid`, and `walkthrough.e2e.ts` moved off a fixed sleep onto an `aria-busy` settle-wait — but neither fix pattern was ever backported to the sibling specs that needed it. None of this was visible to anyone: e2e isn't a required PR check, and the `report-red` job that exists specifically to file a tracking issue on a red nightly has itself errored on every single scheduled run since 07-13 (`defaults.run.working-directory: app` at the workflow level, no `checkout` step in that job → "No such file or directory"), confirmed live this session across the full run history, with zero `nightly-red`-labeled issues ever filed.

The eval "quality" lane (9 scenario YAMLs, a fully unit-tested harness including a genuinely well-built judge≠SUT hard-refuse guard) has never executed against real cognition: `eval/baselines-committed/` is empty by design pending a first promotion run, and `gh secret list` on the repo returns nothing — no `EVAL_COPILOT_TOKEN` — so the weekly `eval-scorecard` job has skipped on every observed run. The harness's own code is proven bug-free; whether Decompose/Connect/Claims/Recall/Researchers/Reflect/Jobs quality is actually good, or has ever regressed, has never been mechanically checked once. Similarly, `signedProtectedFolder.e2e.ts` — the one guard for the still-open MUST issue #56 (macOS TCC vault access) — appears in zero CI workflow and needs a signed build + Apple cert to run at all; given release.yml has run once and failed, it has almost certainly never executed.

At the IPC boundary, of 72 registered `ipcMain.handle('kb:...')` channels, ~30 are never directly invoked by `ipc.test.ts` nor by any e2e spec — including `kb:capture`, `kb:quiesce`/`kb:resume`, `kb:setInstanceSettings`, `kb:setJobConfig`/`kb:runJobNow`, `kb:setAgentModel`. Most of these are covered from both neighboring tiers (renderer call sites via mocked `window.kbApi` in component tests, e.g. `jobsView.test.ts` thoroughly asserts `setJobConfig`/`runJobNow` call args; business logic via `kb/*.test.ts`) — but the thin `ipc.ts` marshaling layer itself, the exact class of bug BUG #65 was, is untested for these channels specifically. Preload↔handler parity is currently clean (verified by diffing `preload.ts` against `ipc.ts`'s registrations — the one preload-only channel, `kb:askProgress`, is a legitimate one-way push event) but has no mechanical guard against future drift.

strengths: Copilot deciders (decompose/claims/compose/connect/reflect/archivist) share one injectable-runner scaffold (deciderScaffold.ts's CopilotRunner) and tests inject canned prompt→response closures that exercise real prompt-building + parsing + validation, not a bypassed decider — the 'test the real agent path' bar is genuinely met.
No assertion-free tests, no unit-tier snapshot tests, and no remaining toLocaleString()-based date assertions anywhere in the suite — prior-review-flagged smells appear fully remediated.

recall.e2e.ts (TEST-21) is a well-designed, deterministic regression guard for a real historical bug (BUG #65): a fake copilot + fake login shell prove the resolveExecutable→forStdio path was actually taken, platform-aware (skips only the positive spawn-marker check on Windows, keeps the negative regression assertion everywhere).

smoke.e2e.ts and walkthrough.e2e.ts already fixed the exact brittle-assertion patterns (exact-copy-string, fixed sleep) that later broke activity/ask/jobs e2e — the right pattern was invented in-repo, just never backported to siblings.
Release-script logic (tagVersion.mjs, verifyRequiredChecks.mjs) has real unit tests covering the release-gating and required-check-evaluation logic, not just the app.
The eval harness's judge≠SUT guard (assertJudgeDistinctFromSut) is a genuine hard refuse on model-id collision, not an audit-after-fact, and is itself unit-tested.
Git-backed integration suites use one canonical gitAvailable signal (test/gitEnv.ts) and describe.skipIf, avoiding the 'silent green on a git-less runner' trap the spec explicitly calls out.
preload.ts ↔ ipc.ts channel parity is currently clean (verified by direct diff) despite no automated guard for it.
open_questions: Has the ci.yml `snapshots` job (showcase.e2e.ts's only real coverage path) ever actually run, or is it in the same 'exists but never dispatched' state as the eval-scorecard and signed-build smoke? Not verified this session.

For the 250 MUST requirements at Verify:none-yet, what fraction (like SPEC-0060's 16) are stale-bookkeeping-but-actually-tested vs. genuinely unbuilt (like SPEC-0035 HEALTH-2..9)? This needs a manual pass per spec; COV-3/COV-5 give a method but not a full accounting.

Does anyone still review walkthrough.e2e.ts's nightly screenshots now that main hasn't moved and no PR triggers a DL/QD sign-off? If not, the walkthrough gate is running but its output-consumption step has quietly lapsed too.
Is there a plan (even informal) to fund a scoped EVAL_COPILOT_TOKEN so the eval quality-lane produces its first real baseline, or is the eval investment considered done/parked?

domains.label: ci
domains.title: CI coverage, gate value vs time & noise
domains.domain: CI coverage, gate value vs time & noise
domains.verdict: The per-PR gate (quick/package/secrets) is genuinely healthy — fast (~3.6min), stable, and tests the right things — but everything downstream of it (nightly, release) is theater: nightly has been 100% red and its own alerting mechanism has silently failed to file a single issue for all 61 runs across 7+ weeks, and release.yml has never once fired via its real trigger in the project's history.
domains.summary:
The required per-PR gate (quick, package build-check, secret scan) is well-designed and healthy: three jobs, ~3.6min/~1-2min/~10s respectively, low variance across every sampled run, correctly pinned as required in the branch ruleset (verified the ruleset's `required_status_checks` contexts match `verifyRequiredChecks.mjs`'s `REQUIRED_CHECK_NAMES` exactly, 3-for-3), and its 72-channel IPC surface is structurally protected by a `KbApi`-typed preload object rather than needing a bespoke parity test (72 `ipcMain.handle` sites == 72 `ipcRenderer.invoke` calls, zero diff). What "green" proves: typechecks, lints clean, unit+coverage pass at ratcheted per-directory floors, the app still packages+asar-bundles on Linux, better-sqlite3 lands unpacked, and no committed secrets. What it does NOT prove: the app ever launches (no Playwright/app-boot step runs pre-merge), macOS-only native-dep regressions (chokidar's fsevents class, #247/#540) on the actual PR, or Windows behavior at all.

The nightly/weekly lane, meant to backstop exactly those gaps, is broken in a way nobody could see. I read `nightly.yml` and confirmed: `defaults.run.working-directory: app` applies workflow-wide, but the `report-red` job (nightly.yml:171-200) has no `actions/checkout` step, so its bash steps try to `cd app` into a directory that was never created — "An error occurred trying to start process '/usr/bin/bash' with working directory '.../app'. No such file or directory." I verified this on the most recent run (100938026285, 2026-09-04) AND the very first nightly run ever (29232073034, 2026-07-13) — the bug has been present since the workflow's inception, 61/61 scheduled runs. Separately, the real jobs it's supposed to report on are also genuinely red: e2e-matrix fails the same 3 specs deterministically on both macOS and Windows every single night (activity.e2e.ts:71 `.activity-empty`, ask.e2e.ts:79 the transcript/citation text, jobs.e2e.ts:76 `.agents-hub-title`/`.job-sub` — I pulled the raw Playwright log and confirmed these are IA-drift, not flakes: 14/17 other e2e specs pass clean, same 3 fail every time). The combination means: a real, deterministic, cheap-to-fix e2e regression has sat unreported for 53 days, and the auto-filer that exists specifically to surface exactly this situation (#525 ENG-1's "red nights file issues" AC) has produced zero issues — `gh issue list --label nightly-red --state all` returns nothing. Additionally, the weekly eval-scorecard — the other pillar of #525 — has never once evaluated anything: `EVAL_COPILOT_TOKEN` was never provisioned, so all 4 sampled Sunday runs short-circuit to a job-level "success" via a bare `::notice::` line, indistinguishable in the UI from a real pass.

release.yml is even less exercised: I found exactly one run in the repo's entire history (28308929235, 2026-06-28), triggered by a branch `push` (not the `v*` tag trigger the workflow actually listens for), with `jobs: []` — a workflow-syntax-level failure before any job was even scheduled. Zero tag-triggered runs exist. The verify/build/publish logic itself is well unit-tested in isolation (`tagVersion.test.ts`, `verifyRequiredChecks.test.ts` — thorough, good fails-before/passes-after coverage), but the actual GitHub Actions integration — checkout the tagged SHA, fetch check-runs, `npm run make` on macOS+Windows, `gh release create --draft` — has never run as a system, not even once. And today, `package.json`'s version is still frozen at `0.1.0` (confirmed), so a `v0.1.0-rc.1` tag pushed right now would fail at the very first `verify` step (RELEASE-6's version-match guard correctly rejecting `0.1.0-rc.1 != 0.1.0`) — which is the guard working as designed, but it also means the entire downstream build+publish path remains completely unvalidated pending a version-bump PR that hasn't happened.

Cost framing needs a correction: the repo is PUBLIC (`gh repo view` confirms `isPrivate: false`), and GitHub Actions minutes are unlimited/free on public repos regardless of runner OS. The whole "CI-COST-REDUCTION" architecture baked into ci.yml's comments — splitting `package`/`package-macos`, making e2e opt-in-by-label — was justified explicitly by "macOS cloud runners bill at 10× the Linux rate... the dominant recurring Actions spend." On the repo as it exists today, that spend is zero dollars. And the opt-in labels this architecture relies on for pre-merge coverage are essentially unused in practice: the `macos` label has been used exactly once ever (PR #564, reactively, after the bug it would have caught was already found another way), and `e2e` has never been used post-#525 (its only 3 historical hits predate the opt-in-label pattern). So the practical effect has been: pre-merge macOS/e2e coverage is gone, the "for free" nightly backstop that was supposed to replace it is invisible and broken, and none of this trades off against real cost on the repo as configured today.

Smaller gaps: no `concurrency:` group anywhere (16 same-branch CI run pairs <15min apart in a 100-run sample, all ran to completion uncancelled); no `timeout-minutes` on any job (default 360min ceiling, notable given this product's own logs show "block timeout reached" and a prior render-process-gone crash during compose); gitleaks installed via unauthenticated curl+tar with no checksum; all `actions/*` pinned by mutable major-version tag, not SHA; CI pins Node 22 while local dev runs Node 24.18 with no `engines` field to catch the class of lockfile drift already logged in project memory; and `npm run knip` exits 1 today (30 unused exports/51 types/3 duplicates) so it cannot simply be flipped to a required gate without a baseline/ratchet mechanism first — it currently sits report-only, silently repeating the same findings nightly with nothing acting on them.

Was EVAL_COPILOT_TOKEN deliberately deferred (a real BYOA credential/budget decision) or simply forgotten once #525 shipped? Memory notes 'starts empty, needs EVAL_COPILOT_TOKEN + dispatch' as a known gap — worth confirming this is still an intentional deferral 7 weeks later.

domains.label: complexity
domains.title: Code complexity & simplification candidates
domains.verdict: Healthier than the raw file sizes suggest — the last review's two big dedup refactors genuinely landed and the shell primitives are real — but the mechanical cause of god-files (the four-file channel tax) was never fixed, five stage drain loops and eight directive stores are still copy-paste, and connectStage.ts has quietly become the new pathological file.
domains.summary:
This codebase is not complex in the usual sense. Nesting is shallow (max depth 7, in exactly four engine files; the shell tops out at 5), there are no callback pyramids, no clever metaprogramming, 0 TODO/FIXME, 2 eslint-disables and 10 `any` across ~46k prod LOC. What it has instead is *volume*: 29,650 lines of code carrying 12,747 lines of comment (0.43 comment/code, 0.47 in src/kb), spread across a handful of files that grew by accretion because the architecture taxes every feature across four files.

Start with the good news, because it is load-bearing. The 2026-07-12 review's two named dedup refactors both landed and I verified them against current main. ENG-7 ("pipeline.ts god-file, AC: <800 lines") is done: pipeline.ts went 2,089 → 509 lines, split into `registries/*ControlPanel.ts` (8 modules, 1,085 lines) behind a shared `registryCrud.ts`, plus `pipelineLifecycle.ts` and `pipelineProjections.ts` (#572/#574), with re-exports so no importer had to change. ENG-8 is done: `deciderScaffold.ts` (176 lines) collapses six copies and fixed two real defects (compose's missing `agentKey`, reflect's missing AgentTrace) as a side effect. `pipelineProjections.ts` runs all four projection stores through one `createProjectionStore` factory — the "projection refresher duplication" the brief asked about is already solved. The shell primitives are genuinely adopted, not aspirational: `emptyState()` in 11 view modules, `renderLoadError` in 14, `createVisibilityPoll` in 5, `ViewHandle` in 12. And `instanceSettingsControlPanel.ts` opens by *arguing* why it does not use `registryCrud` ("NOT a list registry … so this stays bespoke") — a deliberate, documented non-abstraction, which is a better signal than either extreme.

Now the residue. **connectStage.ts is the new pathological file** at 1,668 lines / 26 exports / 9 section-commented responsibilities. Its `connectOne` contains a 365-line `prepare` closure (L599–963) reaching depth 7, and three logically independent sweeps — link promotion, `dedupClaimsOnce`, `linkOrphansOnce`, ~390 lines — that share nothing with the resolver but two worktree helpers and happen to be scheduled by the same drain tail. That split is mechanical and behaviour-preserving against a 1,619-line test file.

**The stage drain loop is copy-pasted five times.** I diffed the class prologues of DecomposeStage / ClaimsStage / ComposeStage / ConnectStage / Orchestrator: 47 non-comment lines are byte-identical in *all five* (`sweepTimer`/`start`/`stop`/`setCap`/`getCap`/`busy`/`currentSince`/`poke`/`runDrains`), and the surrounding rationale comments are verbatim clones too. A repo-wide 8-line-window scan finds 231 duplicated instances, and the hottest file pairs are exactly these (claimsStage~composeStage 35 windows, claimsStage~decomposeStage 29). The three schedulers (job/researcher/intake) repeat the same tick lifecycle a further three times. `pathExists` is defined identically in nine files. `directives.ts` is eight near-identical JSONL stores — `readDisambiguationDirectives` and `readEnrichDirectives` differ only in the type name and two field validations.

**The four-file tax is measured and unfixed.** The prior review correctly named it "the mechanical cause of the god-file" but only the symptom was treated. 41 of the 43 commits that ever touched `preload.ts` also touched `types.ts` *and* `ipc.ts` — 95% lockstep. PR #563 shows the unit cost: one read-only channel (`kb:jobHistory`) = 6 edit sites across 4 files for ~8 net lines carrying zero logic. `ipc.ts` is now 860 lines with `registerIpc()` a single 656-line function registering 72 handlers, 29 of which are ≤3-line passthroughs. There *is* a channel-parity test (#527 ENG-12), so drift is caught — but the typing burden stands, and ipc.ts/types.ts/index.css are now the #2/#3/#4 churn files in the repo.

**CSS carries three parallel token vocabularies.** `index.css` defines `--bg/--card/--fg/--border/--error/...`, `design-system.css` defines `--viz-*`, and a third v3 unprefixed set (`--vellum/--ink/--slate/...`) that the file itself calls "the DESTINATION that retires the instrument-panel `--viz-*` names". Views are 85% migrated (958 v3 uses vs 190 `--viz-*`), but design-system.css's own primitives still hold 119 `--viz-*` references, so the migration is frozen mid-flight — and the hand-mirrored layer has already drifted (`--border: #2c4150` vs `--viz-rule: #2e4350`). Separately, 40 of 583 class selectors in index.css appear nowhere in src (mostly the pre-v3 `.explore-*` block).

The renderer is fine as a stack — string templates are not the bottleneck — but the *re-wire* pattern is fragile: 71 innerHTML sites, 72 direct `addEventListener('click')`, only 7 `closest()` delegations, and 53 non-null `querySelector(...)!` assertions that turn any template edit into a runtime TypeError inside `wire()`.

Refactor risk is mostly low because the harness is real (~1:1 test:prod on nearly every hotspot). The exceptions are precisely where I'd want it most: exploreView 0.45, directives 0.52, `agentDrillIn.ts` with no test at all, and no test module that imports `pipelineLifecycle`/`pipelineProjections` directly.

strengths: Prior review's ENG-7 verifiably landed: main/pipeline.ts went 2,089 → 509 lines, split into registries/*ControlPanel.ts behind a shared registryCrud.ts plus pipelineLifecycle.ts and pipelineProjections.ts (#572/#574), with full re-exports so no importer's path changed. The stated AC (<800 lines) was met.

Prior review's ENG-8 verifiably landed: deciderScaffold.ts (176 lines) collapses six copy-pasted decider launch shapes and fixed two genuine user-visible defects as a side effect (compose's missing agentKey, reflect's missing AgentTrace) — dedup that paid for itself in bugs, not just LOC.

The four maintained projections all run through one createProjectionStore factory in pipelineProjections.ts; the 'projection refresher duplication' this review was asked to look for is already solved.
Shared shell primitives are actually adopted rather than aspirational: emptyState() in 11 view modules, renderLoadError in 14, createVisibilityPoll in 5, the ViewHandle show/hide lifecycle in 12.

instanceSettingsControlPanel.ts opens by arguing why it deliberately does NOT use registryCrud ('NOT a list registry … so this stays bespoke') — an explicit, reasoned non-abstraction, which is healthier than either blanket DRY or silent divergence.
Nesting is genuinely shallow: max depth 7 across the whole engine and only in four files; the entire shell tops out at 5. No callback pyramids, no deeply conditional control flow.

Comment density (0.43 comment/code) is overwhelmingly rationale, not restatement — nearly every non-obvious branch names the incident, issue, or requirement ID that motivated it. This is what makes a 1,668-line file readable by someone who did not write it.

Test harness is ~1:1 with prod on almost every hotspot (connectStage 1,668/1,619; claimsStage 812/1,064; ipc 860/1,019), so most of the refactors proposed here have an adequate regression net already in place.
An IPC channel-parity test (#527 ENG-12, ipc.test.ts:998) mechanically catches preload↔handler drift, which is the one failure mode the four-file tax would otherwise cause silently.
Hygiene markers are excellent for a 46k-LOC codebase: 0 TODO/FIXME, 2 eslint-disable, 10 `any`.
open_questions: Is the v3 CSS token migration still intended to complete (retiring --viz-* entirely), or was it abandoned when main went dormant on 2026-07-13? CX-7's recommendation branches on the answer, and design-system.css's own text asserts the retirement as settled intent.

Is the four-file channel tax (CX-4) worth a channel-table migration before a first public pre-release, or should it wait until the daemon extraction (#531) settles the main/renderer boundary? Doing both means migrating 72 channels twice.

Was ipc.ts's growth back to 860 lines noticed? #528's ENG-7 set an explicit '<800 lines' AC for pipeline.ts and met it, but no equivalent bar was set for ipc.ts, types.ts or connectStage.ts — is a soft size budget wanted in SPEC-0011, which today has no rule at all about file size, function length or duplication?

Does the 0.43 comment/code ratio reflect a deliberate house style (worth stating in SPEC-0011 so contributors match it) or an artifact of agent-authored commits? The distinction matters for whether CX-14's decay is a one-off or a recurring cost.

connectStage's DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS/DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS/LINK_WRITE_MAX_ATTEMPTS are three separate bounded-retry policies in one file, each with its own audit vocabulary. Is that intentional per-concern tuning, or three copies of one policy that should share a helper? I could not settle this from the code alone.

SPEC-0011 declares ENG-7 twice — once under E1 (fast-moving deps) and once under E2 (requirement IDs) — despite the document's own rule that IDs are 'stable IDs, never reused'. Which one is canonical? The prior review's ENG-7/ENG-8 labels refer to neither.

domains.label: architecture
domains.title: Future architecture support & modularity
domains.verdict: Unusually well-layered for its age — the daemon seam (#531) is genuinely close and the IPC contract is machine-checked — but extension is gated by a handful of hand-maintained registration lists, and one of them (stage set-aside dispatch) has already silently dropped a stage.
domains.summary:
This is the healthiest domain I would expect to find in a 3-month-old, 46k-LOC Electron app, and the headline claim of the 2026-07-12 deep review holds up under re-measurement: the engine is not entangled with Electron. I built an import graph over all 239 production modules under `app/src` and computed transitive taint. Exactly 10 modules import `electron`, and the indirect count is **zero** — no module reaches Electron through a chain. All 165 `kb/` modules are clean (the only `kb → main` edges are two test files). More striking than the RFC's own framing: 23 of 32 `main/` production modules are already Electron-free, including the entire orchestration core (`pipeline.ts`, `pipelineLifecycle.ts`, `pipelineProjections.ts`) and all 8 registry control panels. `ipc.ts` is a genuinely thin adapter, not a logic dump: 72 handlers over 428 non-comment lines, median 3 lines per handler, 44 handlers at ≤5 lines and only 4 at ≥20. Import cycles are effectively absent — one genuine runtime cycle (`researchFetch` ↔ `researchWebAgent`) in 239 modules; the other 9 dissolve on type erasure.

The consequence for #531 is that Phase A is much smaller than the RFC estimates. The transport-agnostic server module already exists in substance — it is `pipeline.ts` plus `registries/*` — and the only things standing between it and a headless process are (a) the ~10 genuinely OS-bound channels of 72 (dialog, `shell.openExternal`, clipboard, screenshot, `app.getVersion`), which need to stay client-side, and (b) two modules that hard-code `app.getPath('userData')` at module scope rather than taking it injected: `appConfig.ts:15` and `conversationStore.ts:24`. The correct pattern is already established three lines away — `main.ts:148` injects `userDataDir`, `appEvents`, `crashReporter` into `startTelemetry` precisely "so pipeline.ts stays node-testable". Applying that to two more modules is an S-sized change with no design decisions left open. The RFC's own claim that userData appears "in exactly 2 injectable sites" is now stale — there are 5 `app.getPath` sites and the two that matter are *not* injectable.

The real modularity tax is not coupling; it is **hand-maintained registration lists**. Adding an IPC channel costs a fixed 4-file edit (`kb/types.ts`, `preload.ts`, `main/ipc.ts`, `main/pipeline.ts`), which I verified across four separate channel-adding commits — `kb:exploreProjection` (2f15b6e) touched exactly those four plus one implementation module. That tax concentrates churn: `pipeline.ts` has 102 commits, `types.ts` 71, `ipc.ts` 62, `preload.ts` 43 — the top four files in the repo, and a standing merge-conflict generator that has already caused lanes to route around each other (`libraryIndexRuntime.ts:5-9` documents skipping correct lifecycle wiring explicitly to avoid editing `pipeline.ts`). Adding a *stage* is worse: roughly eight sites, including poke edges hand-coded into other stages' `afterDrain` closures.

That list-maintenance risk is not theoretical. The set-aside recovery dispatch in `pipeline.ts:119-137` is an if/else over three of five stages, typed as `stage: string` (`types.ts:342`) rather than the `StageId` union that already exists in `kb/pipelineStages.ts`, so the compiler cannot enforce exhaustiveness. Decompose has fallen through: it emits `setaside` terminal markers (`decomposeStage.ts:46`), which remove the source from the derived queue permanently, but it has no list/retry/dismiss primitive at all, is not read by the status projection (`pipelineProjections.ts:136-138` covers only claims/connect/archive), is not surfaced in Health or Activity (the marker lands in the per-source `audit.jsonl`, not the vault-wide audit log), and returns "Recovery for the 'decompose' stage isn't supported yet." Net: a source that fails decomposition three times is silently and invisibly abandoned, recoverable only by full replay. Compose escapes this only because `composeBacklog` re-opens its set-asides by a separate route.

Where the codebase invested in machine-checked seams, it worked. The `#527` bidirectional channel-parity test (`ipc.test.ts:1004`/`:1014`) parses `preload.ts` source and diffs it against the real registered handler set in both directions; I ran it and it passes. The `#528` decider scaffold is uniformly adopted — all 6 deciders import `deciderScaffold` and thread `agentKey`. Those are exactly the gates that make a 4-file tax survivable. The gaps are where the same discipline was not applied: the 3 push channels have no parity gate (only the sender literals are pinned by tests, never preload's receivers), and `deciderCatalogCoverage.test.ts`'s `FIXTURES` array is hand-maintained, so a 7th decider that forgets to add itself passes the gate that exists to catch it.

Finally, the read-model story is one discipline (canonical HEAD sha as generation counter) implemented three ways — ProjectionStore, SQLite index, and per-stage HEAD-keyed memos — with no shared invalidation seam. SPEC-0058 STATE-6 ("refresh triggered by the canonical advance") is unimplemented: `refreshGraphProjection` and `refreshTodayProjection` have zero call sites (knip-confirmed), leaving Explore and Today on blind 5s/8s cadences despite a working push channel.

strengths: Engine/Electron separation is real and verified, not aspirational: 0 of 165 kb/ modules import electron, and transitive taint is zero — no module reaches Electron through a chain. The only kb→main imports in the repo are two test files.

23 of 32 main/ production modules are already Electron-free, including the whole orchestration core (pipeline.ts, pipelineLifecycle.ts, pipelineProjections.ts) and all 8 registries/*ControlPanel.ts. The daemon Phase A target largely already exists as a module set.

ipc.ts is a genuinely thin transport adapter — median 3 code lines per handler, 44 of 72 handlers at ≤5 lines. Business logic lives behind pipeline.ts's *ForActive facade, which is exactly the shape a second transport would reuse.

The #527 IPC channel-parity test is a real, machine-checked contract in BOTH directions (no preload method without a handler; no orphaned handler). It parses preload.ts source rather than mirroring a hand-maintained list, and it passes (verified by running it this session).

The #528 decider scaffold was adopted uniformly: all 6 deciders share deciderScaffold.ts for runner/self-repair/model-fallback/AgentTrace, and all 6 thread agentKey — the drift that motivated it (compose's dead model pin, reflect's missing trace) is genuinely closed.

registryCrud.ts factors the identical lock/read/patch-or-insert/commit ceremony behind all four registries (jobs/watch/researchers/intake), so a fifth registry is a thin file, not a copy of the ceremony.

researchWiring.ts is an exemplary single-bridge module: the one place main-tier executable resolution crosses into kb-tier adapters, deliberately covering BOTH researcher entry points so the packaged-PATH bug class cannot reopen at a second seam.

Dependency injection is the house style where it matters — ProjectionStore takes compute/load/save/clock/scheduler/push as deps; startTelemetry takes the Electron bits injected explicitly so pipeline.ts stays node-testable; projectionBroadcast.ts abstracts BrowserWindow behind a structural BroadcastWindow interface.
Cross-boundary constants are single-sourced rather than duplicated: STAGE_ORDER in kb/pipelineStages.ts is imported by both backend and frontend precisely so the two cannot drift.

Code comments carry unusually high architectural signal — deferred wiring, rejected alternatives, and the reason for each deferral are written down at the seam (e.g. libraryIndexRuntime.ts explaining why lifecycle wiring was skipped), which is what makes this review verifiable at all.
open_questions: Is #531 Phase B (utilityProcess) still wanted given that the crash evidence is thin? The only recorded render-process-gone was 2026-06-13 during compose, and RSS dropped from ~320-655MB to ~85-325MB after 07-13. Phase A (transport-agnostic server + IDL) delivers the modularity and headless-run wins on its own; Phase B's justification was crash/memory isolation, which the post-07-13 memory profile weakens.

What is the intended relationship between the SQLite library index and the four ProjectionStores long-term — does the index eventually subsume the graph and Today projections (SPEC-0061 B1 says it 'generalizes the graph projection'), or do they coexist permanently? The answer changes whether ARCH-3 and ARCH-8 are two fixes or one migration, and whether the graph projection's persist/load path is worth keeping.

Should the review-answer model open up (SPEC-0061 B2, agent-defined option sets writing into the directive log) before or after the daemon extraction? B2 changes the shape of several IPC payloads; doing it after Phase A means changing the IDL twice, doing it before means a larger Phase A surface.

Do decompose and compose set-aside items need full retry/dismiss parity with claims/connect/archive, or is the correct v1 simply making them visible (Health finding + Activity event) and relying on full replay? ARCH-1's recommendation assumes parity, which may overbuild.

STAGE_ORDER lists 6 stages ('capture','archive','decompose','connect','claims','promote') but the composition root constructs 9 components and compose is absent from STAGE_ORDER entirely. Is compose deliberately excluded from the canonical stage sequence (because it is a re-entrant enrichment rather than a queue drain), or is this drift? It affects how a stage registry (ARCH-4) would be keyed.

Is there an owner for the 7-week-dormant nightly's e2e drift? Three of the four seams this domain would touch (view mounts, projection push, set-aside surfacing) are exactly what those 3 failing specs assert against, so any modularity work here lands on a lane with no working end-to-end signal.

domains.label: docs
domains.title: Design & documentation accuracy
domains.verdict: Mostly healthy where docs are exercised by process (spec status/frontmatter, eval harness, the v3 mockup) but riddled with unforced drift where nothing checks it — CLAUDE.md's own workflow section is wrong even in the commit that was dedicated to fixing CLAUDE.md, a foundational architecture spec (SPEC-0058) shows zero of its shipped requirements as verified, and there is no README/LICENSE/CHANGELOG at all for a repo whose package.json claims MIT.
domains.summary:
The living-spec system itself (specs/README.md, TEMPLATE.md, SPEC-0000, INDEX.md) is well-designed and, where I could check it mechanically, honest: every one of the 61 rows in specs/INDEX.md has a status that exactly matches its target file's frontmatter (0 mismatches), the requirement-ID/Verify: convention is applied consistently across every spec sampled, and app/eval/'s three READMEs describe an eval harness that is verifiably accurate down to the file — scenarios/ has exactly the 9 YAML files described, cassettes/ has exactly the 1 file described, and the KB_EVAL=1 self-skip guard behaves exactly as documented. design-prototypes/vellum-v3.html is also still the live reference: the shipped NAV_VIEWS array matches its <section id> list 1:1, and the mockup even anticipated IA moves (watched-folders under Settings) that code only caught up to later (#504). In-code module headers sampled across kb/main/shell are consistently accurate and spec-linked, with no pre-Vellum naming found.

Where documentation is not exercised by a process, it drifts and nothing catches it. The clearest example is CLAUDE.md itself: the very last commit on main (19bb68f, #583) was titled "fix corrupted CLAUDE.md" — and even after that dedicated repair, its "Workflows (skills)" section names three skills, /kb-code-review, /merge, /auto-mission, that do not exist anywhere in the actual `.clubhouse/skills/` directory (which holds build, create-pr, go-standby, lint, mission, test, validate-changes), misnames a fourth (/validate vs the real /validate-changes), and never mentions five skills that do exist. This is the single most-read onboarding document in the repo and its central "how work gets done" section is materially wrong.

The second theme is specs that say "draft"/"none-yet" for work that has actually shipped and been tested. SPEC-0058 (UI State Model) is the sharpest case: it is `status: draft` and all 13 requirements (STATE-1..13) still carry the literal unfilled template placeholder `Verify: none-yet → test:` — including STATE-8 (the push channel), which is demonstrably implemented and unit-tested (src/main/pipelineProjections.ts, projectionBroadcast.ts+.test.ts, projectionStore.ts+.test.ts). This directly violates the spec system's own SPECSYS-7 rule ("behavior changes update the relevant spec in the same change") and means a reader of the architecture's foundational spec has no way to tell from the document that most of it has landed. terminology.md shows the same pattern in miniature: `status: draft`, both design gates `pending`, and a "Scrub sites (executor task)" section that reads as a live TODO — but every specific string it names was scrubbed and shipped over two months ago (PR #502).

A third theme is two documents describing the same mechanism disagreeing outright. SPEC-0055's own requirement RELEASE-2 mandates `-beta.N` as the pre-release tag grammar; the one piece of release infrastructure actually built, release.yml, implements `-rc.N` instead and treats `-beta.N` as "a future" convention — neither document points at the other. Similarly, app/eval/README.md tells a reader that `KB_EVAL=1 npm run eval` runs "the full scenario library (library.eval.ts)," but package.json's `eval` script has no file filter, so it actually also pulls in bulkRetry.eval.ts, dedupQuality.eval.ts, enrichQuality.eval.ts, and subjectAttribution.eval.ts via the vitest config's `include: ['eval/**/*.eval.ts']`; and the sibling `eval:enrich` script is a byte-for-byte duplicate of plain `eval` (not scoped to enrichQuality.eval.ts the way `eval:scorecard` is scoped to scorecard.eval.ts) — apparently since the commit that introduced it.

A fourth, smaller theme is stale reference material nobody swept: specs/INDEX.md has a genuine numbering gap (SPEC-0044 was never allocated) with the table itself out of the numeric order it claims to keep (0046 listed before 0045); its own "Reserved / planned" table still lists BRAND/SPEC-0057 as un-graduated two months after that spec was written and shipped against (#402/#406/#580), the only entry in that table not given the `~~struck-through~~ written →` treatment every other graduated entry got; brand/README.md still presents `mockups/the-line.html` as one of only two flagship "live screen" examples of the brand identity, though the Status/"The Line" view it depicts was deliberately deleted from the app 15 days after the brand kit was authored (#523); and the 2026-07-12 deep-review docs (still actively cited by later work) contain claims now factually superseded — e.g. ENG-1's "the only required check is typecheck·lint·unit" — with no supersession marker, unlike the same review's own issue-index table which does mark unrelated pre-existing GitHub issues superseded. Finally, nightly.yml's header comment promises an auto-filed tracking issue whenever a scheduled run goes red — a promise that, per this session's established facts, has been silently false every single day since the workflow's first run (a working-directory bug means report-red itself errors before it can file anything) — the kind of documented safety-net that is worse than no promise at all, because it invites trust nobody should place in it.

None of this blocks a technical release, but the missing README/LICENSE/CHANGELOG at the repo root does bear directly on a first public pre-release: package.json declares `"license": "MIT"` with no LICENSE file anywhere to back it, and there is no entry point for a human contributor or downloader other than the agent-oriented CLAUDE.md and 60+ files of living specs.

The 2026-05-30 → 2026-07-12 sweep of the deep-review docs is itself well-organized: every finding carries file:line evidence, and the issue-index (05) does correctly mark several unrelated pre-existing GitHub issues (#403/#405/#427) as superseded, showing the authors know how to annotate staleness when they do it.
open_questions: Is specs/tools/ (the automated requirement-coverage checker specs/README.md describes as 'not built yet') still intentionally deferred, or should it now be prioritized given 60+ specs and at least one confirmed foundational-spec drift (SPEC-0058)?

Are the specs/research/2026-07-12-deep-review/*.md docs meant to be a permanently-frozen historical snapshot (in which case their staleness is expected and fine) or a living reference that should get periodic supersession annotations — no policy either way is stated anywhere.

Does #579's scope (brand comment sweep) cover brand/README.md's own mockup descriptions (the-line.html), or only in-code comments referencing the pre-Vellum identity? Its acceptance criteria don't say.
Is there an intended reconciliation path for SPEC-0055's -beta.N vs release.yml's -rc.N before the first real release, or is -rc.N meant to be permanently retired once beta lands?

domains.label: deadcode
domains.title: Dead code, orphans & superseded features
domains.verdict: Settled, not out of hand: the one big prior-review debt (the 2,467-line Status/"the Line" cluster) was fully paid off, but the same view-rewrite pattern that fixed it is now leaving a smaller trail of its own orphans (dead CSS, superseded IPC, an unwired safety backstop) that nobody has swept yet.
domains.summary:
This domain is healthier than the raw knip count (44 unused value-exports, 51 unused types, 3 duplicate-export files) suggests. Manual verification of a representative ~20-item sample found the overwhelming majority are false-positive noise: functions/consts genuinely used within their own file but exported wider than necessary (writePerfIndexCache, the watchLedgerPath/readWatchLedger/writeWatchLedger trio, PURGE_DIRS, buildAppearanceConfig), or types consumed structurally without an explicit type-only import (most of the 51). Knip is not wrong that these are "unused exports" — it's right that the `export` keyword is unnecessary — but almost none of it is dead *code*. Three genuinely dead exports were confirmed by full-repo grep: `VIEW_JOBS`/`VIEW_RESEARCHERS` (views.ts) carry a comment claiming "deep-link/back-compat" that is false — shell.ts's route-mount map has no entry for either id, so nothing resolves them — and `resetLibraryIndexRuntimeForTests`, a reset hook built explicitly to prevent store-handle collisions between IPC contract tests, that zero tests actually call.

The best news in this domain is that the prior review's headline dead-code item — the dissolved Status/"the Line" cluster (statusView.ts/.test.ts, lineMotion.ts/.test.ts, theLineModel.ts/.test.ts, theLine.css, ~2,467 lines) — is verifiably gone. `git grep -l 'statusView\|theLine\|lineMotion'` across app/ returns only unrelated hits (pipelineStatusView.ts, lineStations.ts), matching the design spec's own acceptance criterion, and the deletion landed in PR #550 (13f4e48, 2026-07-12). The spec doc itself (`specs/design/vux-old-ui-retirement-523.md`) still carries stale frontmatter (`status: draft`, gate 2 `not-yet-routed`) for work that shipped seven weeks ago — a small living-spec bookkeeping gap, not a code problem.

The new orphans cluster around three view/API rewrites that never got a follow-up cleanup pass. First, CSS: Explore's pre-graph list-based UI (`.explore-center*`, `.explore-neighbor*`, `.explore-sub*`, `.explore-recenter/-edge/-rel/-expand/-more`) was superseded by the SVG-graph rewrite (`exp-*` classes, commit 84f6b95/#501) but never deleted — ~29 selectors, ~40 declaration lines, index.css:884-992. A second, smaller grab-bag (`.ag-empty`/`.ag-loading`, `.job-empty`, `.rdesk-empty`, `.source-slots`) was orphaned when Agents/Jobs/Sources moved onto the shared `emptyState()`/`.viz-empty` primitive; `.ask-hl` styles a highlight span that's never applied anywhere in askView.ts (a feature that was styled but never wired); `.rev-skeleton-line--sub`/`.rev-skeleton-sub` are an unused skeleton variant. I separately verified three template-literal-constructed class families (`gl--${kind}`, `capture-note--${kind}`, `src-mark--${type}`) that a naive grep (mine and, presumably, knip's underlying heuristics) would flag as unused but are fully reachable via their typed unions — a useful caution for anyone acting on this report mechanically.

Second, IPC: five of 72 handled `kb:*` channels (`exploreNeighborhood`, `composeBacklog`, `composeBacklogStatus`, `activityEvents`, `setSourceSensitivity`) have a complete main-handler + preload-wrapper + `KbApi` type + dedicated `ipc.test.ts` coverage, but zero call sites in shell/qcap. `exploreNeighborhood` is clearly superseded (exploreView.ts calls the newer `exploreProjection` instead — SPEC-0058 STATE-2). The other three look like backend built ahead of a UI decision (the same pattern as the #192 set-aside review lane) rather than pure cruft — `setSourceSensitivity`'s read counterpart (`getSourceSensitivities`) IS wired into Activity's lineage view, so users can see a source's sensitivity but have no in-app way to correct it. Preload↔handler parity itself is exemplary (72/72, zero mismatches either direction) — a real strength worth calling out.

Third, and most consequential: the #515 canonical-writer hardening (PR #544) built a Mutex-level section-timeout backstop (`LockSectionTimeoutError`, `Mutex.sectionTimeoutMs`/`RunOptions.timeoutMs`) explicitly documented as covering "non-git work in a section (fs writes, sidecar reads)" — then a same-PR follow-up commit deliberately declined to apply it as a blanket default (a reasonable call for the heterogeneous multi-git-call stage sections) and nothing since has opted any real `Mutex` into it. I confirmed 0 of ~25 production `new Mutex(...)` sites pass a timeout. Concretely, `Orchestrator.capture()` runs `captureToInbox()` — raw, unbounded `fs.mkdir`/`fs.writeFile` calls — under the same shared per-vault lock every pipeline stage uses, with no timeout of any kind; the #163 watchdog only logs at 30s, it never releases the lock. A stalled write (iCloud eviction, a disconnected network vault, a full disk) would wedge every future capture and stage run silently — the exact failure class #515 exists to close, just not closed for this one call site. This is the domain's most actionable finding: the fix (pass `timeoutMs` on the capture `lock.run` call, following the pattern already built and tested) is narrow and low-risk, unlike the broader stage-lock case the #544 follow-up correctly punted on.

Rounding out the list: `showcase.e2e.ts`'s 332 KB of linux-only visual-regression baselines have never actually gated anything — the test self-skips off-linux, both places e2e specs run (ci.yml's opt-in job, nightly.yml's matrix) are macOS+Windows only, and the dedicated linux "snapshots" dispatch job has fired zero times across 1,240 total CI runs; the committed baselines (2026-06-06) predate the wave-2 dark-repoint/v3-conform token overhaul (2026-07-12) they'd need to match. And ~656 KB of tracked design assets are quietly stale: `brand/mockups/the-line.{png,html}` mock up the now-deleted Status view, and `design-prototypes/vellum-ux-v2.html` is superseded by `vellum-v3.html`, the only prototype any current spec cites as source-of-truth.

strengths: The prior review's largest dead-code item (the 2,467-line dissolved Status/'the Line' cluster: statusView.ts/.test.ts, lineMotion.ts/.test.ts, theLineModel.ts/.test.ts, theLine.css) is verifiably and completely deleted — git grep across app/ for statusView|theLine|lineMotion returns zero matching files, matching the retirement spec's own acceptance bar, and views.ts's own comment accurately documents the deletion instead of the stale 'mount is retained' claim the spec flagged as wrong.
preload.ts and main/ipc.ts are in perfect 1:1 correspondence (72/72 kb:* channels) — no dangling handler, no dangling preload wrapper, in either direction.

All four eval/fixtures/ directories (jobs-example, reflect-seed, research-web, corrupted-vault) are live and wired through scenario YAMLs — no orphaned fixture data despite living in a directory a cursory grep would flag as under-referenced.

Three template-literal-constructed CSS class families (gl--${kind} in activityGlyph.ts, capture-note--${kind} in captureView.ts, src-mark--${type} in sourcesView.ts) are all fully reachable via their typed unions/lookup tables when manually traced, despite reading as 'unused' to naive static-string tooling — the dynamic-construction risk the task asked about is present but was not found to hide any actual dead states.

Most of knip's ~100 flagged unused exports/types are exported-wider-than-needed rather than dead logic — a real hygiene nit, not a cleanup backlog; the codebase's actual dead-code footprint is small relative to its 46K prod LOC.
open_questions: Should kb:composeBacklog/composeBacklogStatus (a coverage % + manual backfill trigger) and kb:setSourceSensitivity (per-source override, whose read counterpart IS wired into Activity) get a UI surface, or be deleted as backend-ahead-of-product? This needs a design/product call, not an engineering-only deletion.

Was showcase.e2e.ts's linux visual-regression guard ever intended to gate CI, or was it always conceived as a rare manual pre-release check? If the former it needs a real linux CI leg; if the latter, the README/spec comments should say so explicitly instead of reading like a normal opt-in e2e gate.

Does captureToInbox's raw fs.writeFile path ever actually stall in the field (iCloud/network-vault users)? No crash-report or hang evidence either way was found in the one observed instance's 36K-line log (only mem.sample/mem.leak-suspected events) — worth a synthetic slow-filesystem test to confirm the Mutex-backstop gap is a live risk rather than theoretical before prioritizing a fix.

Is there a broader inventory of which other lock.run(...) sections (beyond capture) perform unbounded non-git fs work that the #544 boundedGit fix didn't reach? The review only traced the capture path in depth.

domains.domain: Reliability & correctness (data loss, corruption, error surfacing)
domains.verdict: Engine-internal reliability is genuinely strong and the July deep review's bug list is 12/15 closed — but the vault boundary is not: the promotion gate is a destructive one-way mirror that silently eats user edits in the live Obsidian folder (empirically reproduced), and engine failures have essentially no in-app surface.
domains.summary:
The engine's *internal* crash-consistency story is one of the strongest parts of this repo. Optimistic concurrency is real and carefully reasoned: `withOptimisticAdvance`/`withConcurrentAdvance` capture a checkpoint, prepare off-lock in a per-item ephemeral worktree, and advance under one per-vault mutex via a single `advanceOrCollide` primitive (ff → disjoint cherry-pick replay → bounded collision retry → set-aside), with a `finally` that reaps the worktree and a prune-guarded branch sweep. Startup reconciles a stale `index.lock` (a triple-gated heal with a pid sidecar) and a stuck `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`/sequencer. `before-quit` now stops the pipeline and awaits a bounded promote flush on every quit path including Cmd-Q. Path containment is centralized and symlink-safe (`pathContainment.ts`), the destructive job write-sink is allowlisted, and the Code researcher's git layer is a structured-op allowlist with option-injection hardening. Audit/journal readers skip torn JSONL lines rather than throwing. I re-verified all fifteen BUG-1..15 items from `specs/research/2026-07-12-deep-review/03-reliability.md`: **12 fully landed, 3 partial** (BUG-1 lock-bounding, BUG-10 unscoped commits, BUG-14 audit walk). Closure mostly did equal landed code.

The problems are at the seams, and the biggest one is the vault boundary. `promote()` (staging.ts:143-144) applies the mainHead↔staging evergreen delta with `git rm -f` for deletions and `git checkout staging -- <path>` for adds/modifies, directly in the vault ROOT worktree — the live folder the README tells the user to "open directly in Obsidian." I reproduced both failure modes in a scratch repo: (a) an **uncommitted** user edit to an entity note is silently overwritten by the checkout, with **zero copies left in git history** — unrecoverable; (b) a user file created under `entities/`/`sources/`/`outputs/` and committed (e.g. by the very common Obsidian Git plugin) appears as `D` in the mirror diff and is `git rm -f`'d out of the vault. Nothing checks the root for divergence before mirroring, and there is no test anywhere asserting a human edit survives a promote. The "edit-quarantine" ruling recorded in the project's own history has no code (`grep -i quarantine` over `app/src` returns nothing). Compounding it, `applyProse` (composeDoc.ts:111-121) *by design* replaces everything between the entity's H1 and its first structured block on every recompose — that region is exactly where a human would annotate — and Connect merges entity clusters **autonomously** (connectStage.ts:908 → mergeNodes.ts:156), deleting loser nodes and their composed prose with no review and no tombstone.

The second cluster is error surfacing. `computePipelineStatus` assembles a rich diagnostic view — `recentErrors`, `lock.state()` incl. the `stuck` flag, worktree inventory, per-stage error flags — and **no renderer consumes any of it**: the only view that calls `pipelineStatusView()` is Reviews, and it reads only `setAsideItems` (reviewsView.ts:153). Status was dissolved in the v3 IA (shell.ts:149-150) and Today's "health" rows are graph lint (dangling/orphans/thin), not engine state. The single remaining engine-error surface is the tray's coarse `✕ Stalled — needs you`. Set-aside recovery covers archive/connect/claims and auto-reopens compose, but **decompose is terminal with no reopen and no list** (`readDecomposeQueue` drops a source at `terminal || failures >= 3`, and `pipelineControlForActive` answers "Recovery for the 'decompose' stage isn't supported yet") — and the observed vault's spans show 13 real `decompose: no JSON object in output` errors plus 8 block timeouts, so sources do die this way, invisibly. The per-stage set-aside badge count is derived from a 25-line dev-log tail, so it disagrees with the actual list.

Third, durability of small state. Only 2 of 14 durable JSON writers use tmp+rename (`writeJsonAtomic`, `canonicalLockMeta`); the 12 registries/ledgers are truncate-then-write, and every reader "self-heals" a corrupt file to empty. For the watch dedup ledger that means re-ingesting every watched file as new **immutable** sources — and the ledger is untracked inside the staging worktree, which `ensureStagingWorktree` `rm -rf`s whenever a one-line `rev-parse` health probe fails.

Finally, BUG-1's greppable invariant ("no `simpleGit(` without a timeout inside any `lock.run` closure") is not actually held: Connect's three lock-held sweeps (`connect:link`, `connect:orphan-link`, `connect:dedup`) each call `ensureWorktree`, which builds a raw unbounded `simpleGit(root)` and spawns 3-5 git children inside the section — and the shared mutex deliberately sets no `sectionTimeoutMs`. Counts: 19 `boundedGit` sites vs 27 raw `simpleGit` constructions; 59 statement-free catch blocks (58 documented, 1 bare) plus 40 inline `.catch(() => {})`.

strengths: Optimistic-concurrency design is coherent and centralized: one `advanceOrCollide` primitive (ff / disjoint cherry-pick replay / bounded collision → set-aside) behind two wrappers, with per-item ephemeral worktrees, a prune+branch-sweep prologue, and a `finally` teardown that falls back to raw `fs.rm` when `worktree remove` fails (canonicalAdvance.ts:136-231).

Ephemeral-worktree reaping is an explicit ALLOWLIST (`archive|claims|connect|decompose|consolidation`-<ULID>), deliberately chosen over a shape match so a persistent `staging`/`job-<id>` worktree can never be destroyed — the comment names the data-loss reasoning (canonicalAdvance.ts:66-81).

The sparse-checkout silent-drop landmine is guarded loudly: after a `sparsePaths` prepare, a non-empty `git status` throws before teardown rather than discarding a write git silently refused (canonicalAdvance.ts:163-171).

Startup reconcile now covers both known wedge artifacts — a stale `index.lock` (triple-gated, pid-sidecar-aware, never clears a live lock) and a stuck `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`/sequencer, with a fail-safe `keep` on an inconclusive external-git scan (canonicalLockHeal.ts:311-354; pipelineLifecycle.ts:377-386).

`before-quit` is wired as the one event that fires on every quit path including macOS Cmd-Q, and holds the quit open for a bounded promote flush (main.ts:188-200; pipelineLifecycle.ts:616-628) — BUG-2's quit half fully closed.

The replay epoch fence is a genuinely good piece of concurrency design: the epoch is captured before the off-lock prepare and re-checked *inside* the same lock the purge holds, so a superseded advance is dropped rather than applied (canonicalAdvance.ts:333-347).

Poison-item handling at archive is now durable and item-scoped: failures are recorded on the unit's own audit.jsonl, the worktree is reset before recording, and an oversize foreign drop is refused with an audited `capture-refused` instead of dead-looping the stage (orchestrator.ts:311-335; ingest.ts:215-282).

Path containment is defined once, symlink-safe, and typed (`checkContainedRel` resolves the deepest existing ancestor), with an explicit Class-A vs Class-B note warning future readers not to conflate rel-containment with id-validation (pathContainment.ts:1-109).

The Code researcher's git layer is deny-by-default: a fixed read-only op set with no raw-subcommand escape, an option-injection guard on every caller value, trusted hardening flags (`protocol.ext.allow=never`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`) and a scrubbed env (codeGit.ts:1-90).

Every audit/journal reader tolerates torn lines: `readArchiveUnitState` (orchestrator.ts:82-86), `readJournal` (jobStage.ts:107-113) and `normalizeAuditLine` (audit.ts:189-228) skip malformed entries instead of throwing — the ENG-15/16 bar is genuinely met on the read side.

Failure comments are unusually good: 58 of 59 statement-free catch blocks carry an explanatory comment naming the condition and why swallowing is correct, and most fixes cite the issue number and the failure they prevent.
open_questions: Is editing the vault in Obsidian a supported workflow or not? The vault README explicitly invites it and the product is pitched as "a second brain over a plain Obsidian/markdown vault", but `promote` mirrors destructively, `applyProse` reclaims the prose region, and Connect merges nodes autonomously. REL-1/2/3 all hinge on this one product ruling, and the recorded 07-05 "edit-quarantine" ratification has no code behind it. If edits ARE supported, the vault root needs a divergence check before every mirror; if they are NOT, the README and first-run copy have to say so, loudly.

Should the shared per-vault mutex get a section deadline now? The `sectionTimeoutMs`/`LockSectionTimeoutError` machinery exists and is deliberately left off (pipelineLifecycle.ts:390-401) with a sound argument — a timeout firing while a git child is still live would recreate the single-writer violation. But once REL-4's unbounded spawns are bounded, every section's git budget IS derivable, and the argument for leaving it off weakens.

Was the `recentErrors`/`lock.stuck` telemetry intentionally orphaned when Status was dissolved in the v3 IA, or is a consumer simply missing? The backend cost (a 25-line dev-log read plus `listWorktrees` on every projection tick) is being paid for data nothing reads, which is either dead weight to remove or a missing view to build — the decision belongs to whoever owns the v3 IA.

How should Full Replay interact with a vault the user has been editing? `PURGE_DIRS` recursively removes `candidates/entities/claims/outputs/reviews/queue` on staging and `git clean -fd` scopes to those trees; any user-authored file inside them is destroyed, and `outputs/` in particular holds saved Ask answers the user explicitly chose to keep. Is `outputs/` really replay-purgeable?

What is the intended durability tier for the working-zone ledgers (`.kb/watch`, `.kb/intake`, `.kb/research`)? They are neither gitignored (so they can be swept into a replay's `git add -A`) nor committed (so they are lost on a staging-worktree rebuild). Picking one — tracked-and-committed like the registries, or explicitly gitignored-and-atomically-written — would resolve REL-7 and part of REL-12 together.
Is a single-instance guard wanted, or is multi-window-on-distinct-vaults a goal? The answer decides whether REL-10 is a two-line `requestSingleInstanceLock` or a per-vault advisory lock file.

domains.label: performance
domains.title: Performance, idle compute, memory, locks & deadlocks
domains.domain: Performance, idle compute, memory, locks & deadlocks
domains.verdict: The July perf wave was real and mostly landed — idle CPU, git spawns, RSS and Ask latency all improved measurably (median RSS 445→210 MB, heapUsed 147→56 MB, idle git spawns ~2,500→~480/hr) — but four of the twelve engine items landed only halfway, and the half that was skipped is the half that scales: an ungated live Health walk every 8s, an unconditional 257 MB/day status-snapshot write, an O(N×(N+M)) backlink pass, and an unbounded `git worktree` call inside the canonical-writer lock that can still wedge the whole pipeline.
domains.summary:
**What the July wave actually closed.** Re-verifying all 36 prior findings (PERF-E1..E12, R1..R15, A1..A9) against `origin/main@19bb68f`: 24 fully landed, 9 partially, 3 not at all. The genuinely-fixed spine is impressive and worth naming. The graph projection is now one walk (N+M+S reads, not N×M) and HEAD-gated through the same `CanonicalQueueCache` the stage drains use (`pipelineProjections.ts:392`), with a reference-equality no-op fast path in the store so an unchanged HEAD costs two small fs reads. The 2.5s status tick lost every one of its git spawns to `fastHeadSha`/`fastHeadBranch` and gained seven HEAD-keyed sub-caches (`pipelineLifecycle.ts:559-567`). Connect's 30s sweep — the "hangs during ingest" mechanism — now HEAD-gates its entire link/orphan/dedup tail (`connectStage.ts:1572`) and byte-stable-prefilters each node *off* the lock (`:1589`); captures got a real priority lane in the Mutex (`stageLock.ts:212`, `orchestrator.ts:463`). Promote applies a `git diff --name-status` delta instead of clear-and-restore (`staging.ts:136`) behind a coalescing debouncer. The activity index reads only appended bytes (`activityIndex.ts:220`). Ask got a process-wide `RecallClient` (killing the per-question CLI-server leak, `ipc.ts:516`), a bounded history window, a 32 KB per-tool-result cap, live `kb:askProgress`, an honest Quick tier via `reasoningEffort`, and a SQLite/FTS5 index with a composite `search` tool. The renderer's whole poll layer collapsed into one correct `createVisibilityPoll`, and `show:false` + route-level code-splitting fixed first paint. The observed instance corroborates it: across 36,037 samples, median RSS fell 445→210 MB and median heapUsed 147→56 MB the day the 07-13 build landed.

**What did not land, and why it matters.** The pattern in the misses is consistent: the *cheap* half of each fix shipped and the *scaling* half was deferred to a fast-follow that never came, and the deferral is written into the code as a comment. Today's 8s composite still calls `buildHealthReport(makeReadOnlyTools(a.vaultPath))` — a live 2N vault walk, ungated by HEAD, with the note "DEV-2's Health re-point will later derive these off the graph projection" one line above (`pipelineProjections.ts:486,495`). Measured on the real vault: 1,534 file reads and 117 ms every 8 seconds forever, ~1.5% of a core at 767 entities and linearly ~19% at a 10k-entity year vault — and it duplicates, on a slower path, what `kb:healthReport` already gets from the SQLite index. The status store writes its 7,426-byte snapshot to disk *every 2.5s* regardless of change (257 MB/day of idle SSD writes): the content-hash gate exists, but only on the graph store, and `projectionStore.ts:87` explicitly notes the no-op branch is "dead weight" for the other three because their computes always build a fresh object. The graph rebuild's file reads were fixed but its backlink inversion was not — it is still `entities × (entities+claims)` substring scans (`graphProjection.ts:149`), measured at 454 ms vs 5 ms for the inverted single pass the fix note specified, a 90× gap that grows quadratically. Sparse-checkout landed for exactly 2 of 10 `withConcurrentAdvance` sites — archive and decompose — leaving claims (per entity×source, the highest fan-out), compose, and connect doing a full-tree checkout per item-attempt.

**Locks.** No `lock.run` section awaits a Copilot call — cognition is genuinely off-lock everywhere, and the priority lane means a capture only waits for the *running* section. But the wedge vector is still open and the code asserts otherwise: `pipelineLifecycle.ts:398` justifies leaving `sectionTimeoutMs` off on the grounds that "every git op in a `lock.run` section now goes through [boundedGit]". That is false — `connectStage.ts:437`'s `ensureWorktree` uses raw unbounded `simpleGit(root)` for `config`, `rev-parse`, `worktree prune` and `worktree add`, and it is the *first* thing `linkOne`, `dedupClaimsOnce` and `linkOrphansOnce` call, all three of which run inside `this.lock.run(...)` (`:1599,1620,1635`) — plus both Health remediation actions. A root `index.lock` held by Obsidian's git plugin or a stray `git` process blocks `worktree add` indefinitely; the section never settles, `pump()` never runs (`stageLock.ts:221` — priority reorders waiters, it cannot preempt), and every stage advance, review answer, settings save and capture queues forever. The #163 watchdog logs `lock.stuck` and sets a status flag, but nothing recovers.

**Idle budget at 1k entities, today.** 13 main-process intervals; ~480 git spawns/hour (4 per 30s, from three stage queue-caches plus Connect's tail gate, all still on the spawning `canonicalHead` while compose and the status caches use the spawn-free `fastHeadSha`); ~11,500 file reads/minute from the Today health walk; 257 MB/day of status-snapshot writes; during ingest, a 4 MB spans re-parse every 2.5s. "Compute tracks mutation" is now true for the graph store and Connect's sweep, and false for status, review and Today — all three of which keep computing, persisting and pushing with no window open at all (macOS tray mode; nothing gates on window presence).
